page: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz. This configuration maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The processor features an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Network baseline throughput is rated at 30 Gbps, while local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs are absent, requiring reliance on networked block storage for persistence.

Performance testing indicates substantial multi-threaded compute capability and high memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in Clang software compilation and static web serving throughput (107.39 GB/sec), as well as a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,499. Single-threaded performance lands comfortably in the top 25 percent across Geekbench and compression tasks, while showing mid-tier metrics under stress-ng. Memory benchmarks demonstrate 196.85 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, though write bandwidth moderates at 80.7 GB/sec. The presence of AMX instructions yields strong prompt processing execution for small and large language models, including 39.74 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the m8i.16xlarge delivers high compute density and cache capacity for multi-threaded enterprise applications without requiring specialized GPU allocations. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on the total reliance on networked storage for disk I/O, which may limit workloads requiring ultra-low latency local scratch disks. The instance is well matched for clustered web serving fleets, enterprise microservices, continuous integration pipelines, relational databases, and in-memory key-value caching such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a balanced general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores running at 3.9 GHz on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 256 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory and a 480 MB L3 cache, the platform delivers strong multi-core throughput and top-tier software compilation performance. The server lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, routing all persistence through remote block volumes, while offering 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Integrated AMX and AVX-512 extensions provide accelerated matrix and cryptographic compute, enabling competent CPU-based LLM token processing. With high throughput across multi-threaded operations, static web delivery, and memory caching, the instance fits enterprise applications, CI/CD compilation, relational databases, and Redis clusters.
